records.finding: Definitions 4-7 treat process paths as adapted random elements, perfect interventions, subsystem solvability and marginalisation. Time splitting and subsampling distinguish lossless re-expression from loss of path information. The manuscript accurately uses this framework for feedback without anticipation and does not infer causal solvability from forecast fit.

Definitions 3/5 and Theorems 3/5/6 require adapted subsystem solutions and the stated regularity for unique solvability, preservation under marginalisation and sigma-separation. Definition 9 and Example 10 explicitly show subsampling as marginalisation and loss of path-level conditional independences. The manuscript preserves these model qualifications; structural interventions still need an operational interpretation.

Definition 2 and Proposition 1 use causal validity plus an actual absolutely continuous intervention law and likelihood-ratio process, including the integrated intensity difference. Theorem 1 supplies sufficient graphical eliminability conditions; simply marginalising a private signal need not preserve causal validity. The manuscript correctly retains mean-one/support/integrability and censoring-intervention conditions.

Definition 3 combines adherence consistency, exchangeability in an enlarged filtration and mean-one likelihood-ratio regularity. The stochastic-exponential adherence weight in equations (10)-(11) and Theorem 1 match the manuscript. Definition 5, Remark 2 and Theorem 2 distinguish regime-specific g-formula laws from broader compensator-invariance changes; the manuscript does not infer support for arbitrary exact-time interventions.

Definitions 1-2 distinguish treatment-mark interventions from changes to treatment scheduling. The main canonical gradient retains the treatment-monitoring mechanism in the nonintervened law. Theorem 2 explicitly assumes a small empirical score/remainder, Donsker membership and mean-square convergence; the manuscript does not silently replace these by generic cross-fitting or arbitrary-learner guarantees.

Assumptions 2.1-2.5 and Proposition 2.1 restrict the generalized Wald ratio to weighted marginal effects over instrument-responsive treatment margins. Date-specific complier recovery additionally uses deterministic status and local comparison/smoothness assumptions 2.6-2.8. The manuscript correctly avoids granting arbitrary strongest-first-stage date selection ordinary full-sample inference.

Assumptions 2.1-2.5 include oracle dependence/moment conditions, orthogonality and explicitly conditional plug-in stability under dependent cross-fitting. Assumption 2.4 acknowledges that adjacent disjoint blocks do not suffice and additional neighbor deletion may be necessary. The manuscript accurately preserves stability as an assumption rather than deriving it from index separation or stationarity.

ITSY is a linear first-order stationary causally sufficient SVAR with a contemporaneous DAG and MCAR grid omissions. The transformed residual covariance and structural-coordinate weighted correction on p7 support the manuscript algebra. The source itself excludes informative missingness, asynchronous clocks and latent confounding from its evidence scope, matching the bank-visit qualification.

The VAR-residual spectral router chooses sparse PDS filtering or pervasive spectral correction. The lag-zero persistence/orientation rules are expressly heuristic and the router separation proof is referred to an extended version. The manuscript accurately refuses to infer causal sufficiency from residual low rank or banking validity from synthetic graph recovery; it retains hidden-state and observation-law distinctions.

TS-ICD orders temporal and contemporaneous independence search and states soundness/completeness for its stationary SVAR setting with a perfect CI oracle relative to independence implications in its underlying MAG. The manuscript does not transfer that guarantee to stronger time-series equivalence restrictions or claim finite-sample bank identification from faster orientation.

The finite observed-state SCM has fresh stage-specific latent confounders; persistent hidden traits are outside scope. Local Manski sets, supported singletons and unsupported successor simplices match the manuscript. Theorem 3.8 makes only the unmodified default family causally sharp under its maintained model; Proposition 3.5 and Theorem 4.4 optimize a rectangular class. The manuscript correctly distinguishes this from globally compatible bounds under persistent hidden-state coupling.
